summary: Renaming a layer in the layers list renames it. Since the evening of 2026-09-17 it quit the app instead, every single time, taking the open document with it.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Flags are on by default; nothing to switch on.

try.do: Draw two rectangles and an ellipse on a blank canvas.
Double click the first row's name in the layers panel, type Header, press Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: Press Command Z and check the row says Rectangle again.
Open a screenshot, pick the Background row, run Separate into Layers, and wait for the rows to stop saying Text 1 and start saying words.
Double click one of those rows, type a name, press Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed while the Mac was locked. The window is the real one, drawn and driven normally, with two known costs: colours can read dimmed, and a tutorial card does not draw at all because the login window is over it.

try.do: Press Command Z and check the row goes back to saying the words that were read off it.
Open the rename field on any row and press Return without typing: the name must not change.

evaluate: Does renaming feel instant, or is there a pause between Return and the row changing?
After renaming a separated run, does undo put back the words that were read off it rather than a number?
Pressing Return on an untouched field leaves the name alone. Is that what you expect, or would you rather it pinned the name it was showing?
Is anything else about the layers list still behaving oddly after last night?
rough: The whole walk set has not been run against this. The seven walks that this crash killed all pass again, and the unit suite is green at 8285 tests, but a sweep is asked for and runs between tasks.
The pictures here were taken with the Mac's screen locked, so colours read a little dimmed. The window, the rows and the names in them are real.

An edit is now worked out and then recorded as two acts rather than one call. Nothing about it is visible, and it costs nothing extra, but it is a rule a future command has to follow: a command that reads the document while editing it must use the two acts. The rule is written on the one call it replaces.
